answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit work or vote. Rewards accrue only after independent checks, while provable fraud burns the deposit and can exclude related accounts. Splitting one actor into a swarm of sybils then multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying influence cheaply; the attacker must fund every identity and keep deposits tied up through each voyage. Like an oasis ringed by a reef, the barrier is costly to cross, though it cannot stop an attacker willing to pay.
